- Page counts: Page 1 says "This certificate includes 2 pages", page 2 says "This certificate includes 3 pages", page 3 says "This certificate includes 3 pages". So page_total = 3.

The scheme: R106 is automatic rail weighbridges. The scheme — the certificate doesn't explicitly mention scheme A or B... OIML-CS scheme. Since this is a pattern approval with test reports, typically scheme A. But the instructions say "scheme (A|B)". The document doesn't explicitly say. Hmm. The certificate relates to OIML R 106 which predates the OIML-CS scheme. I might omit scheme or set to null. Rule 8 says don't fabricate. I'll omit scheme or set null. Actually the schema says scheme (A|B) for certificate. If not present, omit. I'll omit.

oiml_issuer_id: Not explicitly present. The issuing authority is National Measurement Office (UK). There's no explicit issuer ID like "01" or "UK". Omit.

Category: This is a rail weighbridge (automatic rail weighbridge per R106). Category options: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... Rail weighbridge → "Automatic rail weighbridge" or "Weighing instrument". I'll use "Automatic rail weighbridge" — the category is free text with examples. R106 is "Automatic rail weighbridges". So category: "Automatic rail weighbridge".

Type designations: ["Railweight TSR4000"]. Also transducer type "Weighline" is a component.

Components: Transducer type Weighline, Emax = 15,000 kg. Max. no. of weighline transducers: 16 (8 pairs). Also alternative load cells may be used (any compatible R60 load cell). Also Advantech PCI-6873 motherboard and Enhance 200W Micro ATX power supply unit mentioned for one power supply configuration.

Actually accuracy class is "≥ 0.5" and "≥ 0.2" — the class is 0.5 or better for coupled wagons, 0.2 or better for total train. The recommendation section says "for accuracy class: 0.5 (coupled wagons) or 0.2 (total train)". I'll do config_level: attribute "accuracy_class", axis "weighing_mode", values: [{condition: "coupled wagon weighing", value: 0.5}, {condition: "total train weighing", value: 0.2}].

Wait, the table says "≥ 0.5 (coupled wagon weighing)" — meaning accuracy class better than or equal to 0.5. Hmm, for rail weighbridges, class 0.5 or 0.2. The "≥" here likely means the class number... Actually in OIML, accuracy class 0.2 is more accurate than 0.5. "≥ 0.5" seems odd but I'll extract as given: value 0.5 with min semantics? Let me just record value 0.5 and 0.2 per condition. Actually the table literally has "≥ 0.5 (coupled wagon weighing)" and "≥ 0.2 (total train weighing)". Hmm, that would mean class ≤ 0.5? I'll keep the value as 0.5 and 0.2 respectively. Maybe include the ≥ as... The structured value rules: ranges with ≥ become {min: X, max: null}. But accuracy class isn't really a range. I think it's cleaner to record value as number. But to be faithful, maybe {min: null, max: 0.5}? That would mean class 0.5 or better numerically... ugh. The header text says "for accuracy class: 0.5 (coupled wagons) or 0.2 (total train)" without ≥. I'll use plain numbers 0.5 and 0.2 in config_level, and for the type-level accuracy_classes in recommendation: [0.2, 0.5].
